method: Claude's rating: crowd score weighted by review volume, plus awards and guide listings, spread onto a 5-star scale.

venues.area: Tarmonbarry: public moorings by the bridge

venues.name: The Purple Onion
venues.note: Lively restaurant by the bridge, among the best on the Shannon, reviewers say: seafood landed daily at Killybegs, Monaghan Wagyu, rump of lamb, fish tacos, home baking such as the bakewell tart; music and great service. Taste of the Waterways award 2024. Popular; book a table.

venues.name: Keenan's
venues.note: Landmark pub, restaurant and boutique hotel by the bridge, with a cosy bar, a conservatory and a brighter room out the back; busy at lunch, so book. Compact menu done well: the garlic steak sandwich is famous, also Thai green curry, chicken dishes, soup and toasties. Day menu 12:00–17:00 Mon–Sat, evening 17:00–20:30 Mon–Sat, Sunday menu 12:00–19:30 (its own menus page, Nov 2026). Taste of the Waterways award 2011.

venues.name: Cox's Bar
venues.note: Pub: no food advertised. Very traditional, family-run bar by the river with a good pint, a friendly landlord and locals keen to talk about the village's history.

venues.name: Cox's Steakhouse
venues.note: Cosy steakhouse on Harbour Road, a favourite of boaters: big portions, the signature steak sandwich, steaks and lamb cutlets; a few reviewers had a poor meal. Food served 08:00–21:00, à la carte from 17:00.

venues.name: The Brandywell
venues.note: Welcoming pub, restaurant and guesthouse on Main Street: fresh, well-presented food in generous portions at good value, a great pint of Guinness and a relaxed bar. Restaurant food 17:00–21:00; bar food all day; afternoon tea by booking.

venues.name: Tasty Bites Drumod
venues.note: Takeaway: pizza, kebabs and chips in big portions. Reviews vary widely, with slow service when busy.

venues.name: Duignan's Bar
venues.note: Pub: no food. Friendly little local with a great pint; the shop attached has driven boaters and their shopping back to the boat.

venues.name: Taylors
venues.note: Pub: proper family-run local with warm owners, the best Guinness around, a pool table and an outdoor area at the back. A reviewer had burgers here, so food is sometimes served; ring ahead.

venues.name: The Cottage Restaurant
venues.note: Small fine-dining cottage restaurant, named Best Restaurant in Connaught 2026 (its own Instagram): Malaysian-born chef Sham Hanifa mixes Asian cooking with Irish produce. Four-course set menu for €60 (Wagyu supplement), cod and duck praised; Sunday lunch. Excellent service, only about 25–30 seats; book ahead.

venues.name: The Boat House
venues.note: Café in Mercantile Plaza by the marina; order at the counter. Breakfasts, shakshuka, Leitrim boxty, toasted sandwiches, burgers, good vegetarian sausages and home-made cinnamon buns and desserts; service can be slow when busy.

venues.name: The Boardwalk Restaurant
venues.note: Café bar and restaurant in the Landmark Hotel overlooking the Shannon: consistently good food, with Sunday lunch (salmon) and desserts praised; friendly, attentive service, comfortable seating. The lunch menu says Monday to Saturday 12:00–16:00.

venues.name: The Oarsman
venues.note: Award-winning gastropub on Bridge Street with local, organic and Irish artisan produce: its seafood chowder was a Michelin Guide inspectors' dish of the month (Aug 2026), with fish tacos, featherblade of beef and tiramisu; strong wine list, gluten-free handled well. Lunch Thursday to Saturday from 12:30. Closed Sundays (except bank holidays), Mondays and Tuesdays: its site's notice says so, though its hours list still shows Tuesday evening.

venues.name: Francesco's Italian Takeaway
venues.note: Clean town-centre chipper a stone's throw from the quay, often called the best in Carrick: fresh cod and proper chipper chips in generous portions, plus pizza; friendly counter staff and some seating. Good for chicken too: reviewers praise the southern fried chicken and the crumbed chicken fillet burger, one calling it the best they had eaten.

venues.name: Carrick Cafe
venues.note: Clean, friendly café in Mercantile Plaza: breakfast, lunch, fresh salads and good coffee by day, and sushi (smoked salmon rolls) to take away; reasonable prices.

venues.name: Di Vino Italian Restaurant
venues.note: Family-run Italian trattoria on Bridge Street with a daily lunch menu and great value: spaghetti pescatore with prawns, squid and mussels is the dish people rave about; soft pizza and garlic bread, fresh juices and Aperol. Good with children.

venues.name: Vitto's Restaurant & Bar
venues.note: Spacious, well-decorated Italian and Irish restaurant in the Market Yard: steaks, stuffed chicken, carbonara, beef stroganoff, prawns, bruschetta and cheesy garlic bread; friendly floor staff. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

venues.name: The Olive Tree
venues.note: Cosy café and wine bar in the Market Yard with exposed stone and a quiet courtyard, often rated the best breakfast in the area: full Irish with excellent sausages and black pudding, bagels, pancakes, scones and carrot cake, very good coffee; takes groups. Vegetarian and vegan options.

venues.name: Sonnies Coffee House
venues.note: Cafe: breakfast bagels, sandwiches, wraps, soup. Listed as permanently closed (Nov 2026).

venues.name: Flynn's Bar
venues.note: Welcoming, much-loved bar on Main Street, Connacht Pub of the Year 2018 and 2022 (its own Instagram), with a cosy heated area at the back you can book, a famous pint, wings and pizzas, weekend music and the football on.

venues.name: Sliced Wood Fired Pizza
venues.note: Small wood-fired pizzeria, rated the best pizza in the area by a wide margin: excellent dough, four-cheese pizza, crispy wings, salads; drinks brought in from the pub next door. Great value, friendly staff.

venues.name: BR Bistro & Bar
venues.note: Cosy, family-run bistro, wheelchair-accessible, with the owners on the floor: steaks cooked to order, prawn and chorizo pil pil, beef kofta, burgers and good desserts; on the pricier side and a few dishes disappoint. Family friendly.

google: An Poitín Still Bar, Restaurant & Accommodation Carrick-on-Shannon
venues.name: An Poitín Still
venues.note: Big, lively bar on Main Street with live bands at night, popular with stag and hen parties; strict door staff. Food is reasonably priced but reviews are mixed. No food Wednesdays or Thursdays.

venues.name: Shudh Indian Restaurant
venues.note: Comfortable Indian restaurant in The Courtyard off Main Street: fresh, authentic cooking in good portions at fair prices, with the garlic, coriander and onion naan singled out. Friendly staff; booking recommended. Evenings only.

venues.name: Buffalo Boy
venues.note: Restaurant with an open kitchen, good for a date or a family celebration: T-bone and other steaks cooked to order, lasagne, beef 'cigar' starter and good cocktails. Smooth, friendly service.

venues.name: Murtagh's Bar
venues.note: Busy bar and late-night venue, a favourite for stag and hen groups, with a nightclub and cocktail classes. Bar food and finger food are well reviewed and the staff are friendly; loud and crowded at weekends.

venues.name: Square Corner
venues.note: Tiny, cheerful family-run pizza and pasta place with walls and ceiling covered in children's drawings, crayons and board games: home-made pizza, pasta cooked to your taste and a standout garlic pizza bread, at low prices. Lovely owners; good for families.

google: My Kitchen by Sham Hanifa Carrick-on-Shannon
venues.name: My Kitchen by Sham Hanifa
venues.note: Spacious, modern café-restaurant from chef Sham Hanifa (The Cottage) in the retail park on the Cortober side, with free parking: breakfast, lunch and evening menus with an Asian lean (rice bowls, ramen, beef stir-fry) alongside soups, sandwiches and house-made cakes and scones; guest-chef evenings. Service can be disorganised when busy.

venues.name: Gings Bar
venues.note: Pub: newly reopened after four years and beautifully restored in its original stonework, with one of the best riverside beer gardens in Ireland on the Cortober bank, a covered outdoor area and many screens for sport. No food.

venues.name: Cryan's Teach Ceoil
venues.note: Pub: homely bar with some of the best trad music around (Thursday to Sunday year-round), the best pint in town, a great owner and a mix of locals and boat crews. Food all day in the adjoining Regatta Bar at Cryan's Hotel (lunchtime carvery, evening menu). Phone and menus are for Cryan's Hotel, whose Regatta Bar serves the carvery.

venues.name: The Barrelstore
venues.note: Pub: smart, clean bar on Bridge Street with a beer garden, live music, quiz nights and good cocktails; pizzas, snacks and nibbles menu. Busy at weekends.

venues.name: McHugh's Bar
venues.note: Pub: big, lively bar on Bridge Street with live bands from the afternoon at weekends and a disco bar with dance floor at the back; a great pint and a good bouncer. Packed and loud on bank holidays and with stag and hen groups. No food advertised.

venues.name: Dunnes Bar
venues.note: Pub: late bar with a huge outdoor area at the back, busy with groups at weekends. No food advertised. Popular with locals.

venues.name: Gracie's Bar
venues.note: Pub: late-night bar on Main Street, a favourite for hen parties, with music, fast bar service and friendly bouncers who keep an eye out. Street-food menu on its own site.

venues.name: The Tipsy Tailor
venues.note: Pub: intimate lounge bar with a fire, a well-kept pint, good hot whiskeys and friendly staff; live music Friday and Saturday nights and the rugby on, with free finger food during big matches (its own Instagram); dog-friendly. No menu advertised.

google: The Leitrim Inn & Blueway Lodge Leitrim
venues.name: The Leitrim Inn
venues.note: Friendly pub, restaurant and lodge by the harbour, ideal for mooring overnight. Big breakfasts, good bar food and Sunday lunch; music sessions on Friday and Sunday nights, when sandwiches have been handed round free. Breakfast daily 9:00–12:00; lunch/dinner 12:00–20:30.

venues.name: MJ O'Connor
venues.note: Pub: the old Carty's bar, redone in an old-world style, on the Shannon at the start of the Shannon–Erne canal, with a games room with darts, an outdoor area and live bands at the back. Serves pizza, burgers and chips; young and loud at weekends but all ages welcome.

venues.name: Donnellans Lounge Bar
venues.note: Pub: seventh-generation family-run lounge bar, spotless, with excellent pints, welcoming music sessions and some of the friendliest locals on the river. No food advertised.

venues.name: The Waterfront Restaurant
venues.note: Restaurant at the private Cootehall marina with views over the water: well-presented food (crispy Brie, lamb parcel, lamb shank, steaks, BBQ ribs) and warm, professional service. Fills up; book ahead. The public quay is a few minutes upstream.

venues.name: M.J. Henry
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food or hot drinks. A rare old bar with a turf fire in the lounge, a great pint and a warm welcome for boaters; easy to reach from the river.

venues.name: Italian at Tara Marina
venues.note: Italian restaurant and cosy bar by the river at Tara Marina: bruschetta, garlic mushrooms, pasta, top-notch pizza, gelato and a children's menu, in large portions; live music some nights. Service can be slow. Its own Instagram (Jul 2026) gave Wednesday to Saturday 17:00–22:00, Sunday 13:00–22:00. Listed as temporarily closed (Nov 2026); ring ahead.

google: Lough Key Forest & Activity Park Lough Key Forest Park
venues.name: Lough Key café
venues.note: Café-restaurant in the park visitor centre by the harbour: good, reasonably priced food (toasties, hot meals, ice cream) with a terrace where dogs are welcome; buying something there gets you free parking. Daytime only. Food service ends an hour before the park closes (summer park hours 10:00–18:00, to 19:00 in July–August).

venues.area: Boyle: Boyle Harbour, at the head of the Boyle canal, about 1 km from the town centre

venues.name: An Craoibhín
venues.note: Pub: family-run gastro pub on The Crescent; open from 09:00. Irish breakfasts in the morning, a lunch menu of traditional dishes like roast beef, bacon and cabbage and curry, and a main menu of steaks, salmon and pasta, with starters. Book ahead. Skipper's review: “Usually arrive at rush hour and still get shown straight to a snug table. Service is attentive, friendly, professional and quick. The food is traditional pub grub done very well: the curry is basic, rice and chips, and exactly right for it; the roast beef is a big plate. The room is warm and mixed – workmen, tourists, locals and professionals all squeezed in together, squinting at the blackboard menu. One visit, a visitor asked hopefully about lamb, expecting nothing, and was offered the lamb stew. He was delighted. When I left he was halfway through it and in heaven.”

google: Lovage at the Gate Lodge Boyle
venues.name: Lovage at the Gate Lodge
venues.note: Small, quirky, award-winning family café on Bridge Street in the old gate lodge of King House, looking over the river. Fresh, healthy cooking: well loved for vegan and vegetarian dishes (the plant-based omelette), omelettes, garlic bread, good strong coffee and wine. Warm staff; outdoor seating. Hours vary by season; Friday and Saturday may run to 21:00 or 22:00 in summer.

venues.name: The Bazaar
venues.note: Café and bistro on The Crescent, long and roomy inside, with a covered, dog-friendly garden at the back. Extensive menu: falafel and bhaji pitta (the must-have), fresh-made chicken and waffles, tuna melt, soup and daily specials, organic coffee and treats. Service slows at brunch. Open Monday to Saturday 09:00–18:00, closed Sundays.

venues.name: King House Tea Rooms
venues.note: Tea rooms inside the grounds of King House on Military Road, handy for Boyle Abbey: famous Irish breakfasts, pancakes, soups, sandwiches, wraps, tartlets and moist carrot cake; quick, warm service. Outdoor tables by the house for dogs. Monday 09:00–16:00, Tuesday to Saturday 09:00–17:00, closed Sundays.

venues.name: The Patrick's Well
venues.note: Pub: very clean, traditional local pub on St Patrick's Street with a warm welcome, a good pint and a lively crowd for GAA matches. Drinks only; no food.

venues.name: Creighton's
venues.note: Pub: lovely owner-run bar on Shop Street, decorated with care in old-world style, with a superb pint and hosts (Eddie and Sylvia) who make everyone welcome; outdoor smoking area. Opens 16:00. No food advertised; ring ahead.

venues.name: Roberto's
venues.note: Takeaway on The Crescent: pizza, very good chips, fish and chips and big doner trays at fair prices; one reviewer had a bad meal. Opens 16:00. Delivers to Boyle harbour; say you're on a boat.
